title: Aurora Health - Redwood Implementation Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Aurora Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered goals, timeline for dedicated/private deployment options, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, audit logs), pilot success criteria, and immediate next steps: share onboarding checklist, SOC2 and SSO docs, schedule technical deep-dive for infra team, and provision a short dedicated trial for benchmark tests.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ivy Zhang (Redwood CSM), Samir Rao (Aurora Head Eng), Elena Morris (Aurora VP Product), Priya Desai (Cloud Infra Lead), Jordan Lee (Security)

[00:00:05] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give a quick agenda — intro, goals, timeline, security checklist, and next steps. Uh, if anyone wants to add something shout now.

[00:00:22] Samir: Thanks Maya. Quick note, we're coming off a two-week evaluation of the hosted API, team liked the latency but we, uh, need more control for PHI workflows so exploring Dedicated or Private options.

[00:00:38] Elena: Yep, product wants to start with triage automation and discharge summary drafts. Success for us is 70% automation of initial drafts and less than 2 second per-request latency in production-critical paths. Those are our high level KPIs.

[00:01:05] Maya: Perfect, that helps. Carlos, maybe you can give a quick overview of options and what a typical implementation timeline looks like?

[00:01:12] Carlos: Sure. So Redwood offers three modes — Hosted API for fastest time-to-value, Dedicated reserved capacity which gives you predictable throughput on our GPU pools, and Private deployment for VPC/on-prem for regulated data. For PHI we usually see customers pick Dedicated with VPC peering or Private if they need full on-prem. Typical kickoff to pilot is 4-6 weeks for Dedicated, Private can be 6-12 weeks depending on network and on-prem constraints.

[00:01:53] Priya: When you say VPC peering, are you supporting customer-managed KMS and bring-your-own-keys? That's a hard requirement for us.

[00:02:04] Carlos: Yes, we have KMS integrations and we can support customer-managed keys. For Private deployments you can use your HSM, we also produce audit logs and SOC2 artifacts.

[00:02:18] Jordan: Can you send the exact matrix of controls you've got? We're especially interested in encryption in transit, at rest, and key rotation audits.

[00:02:26] Ivy: Absolutely — we'll share SOC2 Type II report, our security whitepaper, and a KMS integration guide after the call. I'll drop links into the follow-up email.

[00:02:40] Maya: On timeline — if Aurora wants Dedicated trial we can stand up a small reserved pool and run benchmarks within the first week. Carlos will coordinate the benchmark tests and we'll provide a template spreadsheet for results.

[00:02:55] Samir: That sounds good. For benchmarks, we care about p99 latency more than average — can you capture that and also the cost per 1k tokens for the profile?

[00:03:08] Carlos: Yes, we'll include p50/p90/p99 and cost breakdown. We also recommend running tests with your typical sequence length and KV cache usage — that changes results a lot.

[00:03:24] Elena: A quick question about quantization — we've been experimenting in house. How does Redwood's runtime handle quantized models vs fp16? Any tradeoffs in quality we should expect?

[00:03:36] Carlos: Great question. Our runtime supports quantized variants and we produce model recommendations per workload. Often quantization drops cost by ~2-4x with minimal quality impact for many tasks, but we'd validate on your prompt set. We'll recommend a quantization profile in the evaluation.

[00:03:56] Priya: One of our constraints is egress and data residency — all patient data must remain in the region. Do you have regional deployments in us-west-2?

[00:04:05] Maya: Yes, we have hosted in multiple regions and Dedicated can be pinned to region. For Private on-prem, that's obviously local. We'll capture region in the onboarding checklist.

[00:04:21] Jordan: Also, SSO and RBAC — we need SCIM + SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC for token scoping.

[00:04:29] Ivy: That's supported. We offer SSO via SAML, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls. We'll include steps to set up your IdP.

[00:04:40] Samir: Ok, great. Let's talk scope for the pilot — product wants triage automation plus a reranker for our search results. We want to run these in parallel so we can measure end-to-end improvements.

[00:04:54] Carlos: We can do that. Typical pilot scope: 1) triage generation service with a pinned model, 2) reranking using embeddings + a light reranker model. We recommend a canary rollout to 10% of traffic first, then ramp. For reranking, caching embeddings will reduce cost significantly.

[00:05:16] Elena: For the canary, what's the rollback story if latency spikes?

[00:05:21] Carlos: We provide automatic fallback policies — route to a cheaper/older model or to hosted baseline, and you can set latency-based circuit breakers in our routing layer.

[00:05:33] Priya: Network connectivity for Dedicated — will you require us to open ingress from a set of IPs or is it all via peering?

[00:05:39] Carlos: We prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink in cloud setups. For on-prem we support direct peering or site-to-site VPN. We'll send the exact firewall and peering firewall rules in the infra doc.

[00:05:55] Jordan: Audit logs — format and retention? We need at least 12 months and JSON formatted logs for SIEM ingestion.

[00:06:03] Ivy: We can do 12 months with the audit-log add-on. Logs are JSON and we provide a delivery mechanism — S3 or your logging endpoint.

[00:06:14] Samir: Okay, something about pricing — how does Dedicated sizing work? We're trying to model cost vs expected throughput.

[00:06:22] Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity; we size the GPU pool based on your QPS/sustained throughput. There's a monthly commit. For initial pilot we can provision a small pool and you only pay the trial seat for the first month. We'll send an estimate based on your expected token volumes.

[00:06:40] Elena: Any hidden costs we should watch for? Networking egress or data transfer between regions?

[00:06:46] Maya: We'll call out networking egress costs separately. For Dedicated, egress in cloud is charged at cloud rates; we'll provide an estimate. No other hidden fees — optional add-ons like extended log retention or premium SLA are billed separately.

[00:06:59] Priya: For Private deployment, who runs the control plane? We prefer customer-managed control plane where possible.

[00:07:07] Carlos: For Private you can run a customer-managed control plane or a hybrid mode. We'll share the architecture doc with the options and recommended patterns for upgrades and patching.

[00:07:18] Elena: Ok, good. Could we also get a template for rollout runbooks? Our ops team wants step-by-step.

[00:07:24] Ivy: Yes, we have runbook templates and a sample incident playbook. I'll attach those.

[00:07:32] Maya: Sounds like we have the required inputs. Let's align on success criteria — Elena mentioned 70% automation and <2s latency. Samir, any additions?

[00:07:45] Samir: Also include error budget targets — <0.1% 5xxs and 99.9% availability for the pilot endpoints.

[00:07:53] Maya: Great — we'll include that in the pilot SLA.

[00:08:01] Elena: Who will be our primary contacts for day-to-day?

[00:08:05] Maya: Ivy will be your CSM lead, Carlos will manage technical setup and benchmarks, and I'll be overall owner on the account for commercial questions.

[00:08:14] Priya: For the benchmark tests, what do you need from our side? Sample prompts? Production-like traffic?

[00:08:19] Carlos: Ideally you provide a prompt set (5-10 representative prompts), typical sequence length distribution, and a small traffic replay or synthetic load shape. If you can't share real PHI, synthetic but representative is fine.

[00:08:34] Jordan: On data handling — during benchmarking will any data persist on Redwood? We need guarantees around ephemeral storage and no training.

[00:08:42] Carlos: We do not use customer data to train models. For benchmarks we can enable ephemeral cache and clear KV caches after runs. We'll document retention policies.

[00:08:54] Maya: I want to call out a few deliverables we'll send in the follow-up: onboarding checklist, SOC2 and security whitepaper, infra peering guides, benchmark template and cost model, and the pilot statement of work.

[00:09:10] Elena: Timeline — if we start next week what's realistic?

[00:09:14] Maya: If you sign the pilot SOW by March 9, we can provision dedicated trial by March 15, run benchmarks week of March 15-19, and aim for a canary deployment by end of March. Private would add extra time.

[00:09:29] Samir: That fits our Q2 goals.

[00:09:33] Priya: A few nitty-gritty: do you support health checks and circuit breakers at the endpoint so our service mesh can observe failure modes?

[00:09:41] Carlos: Yes, we expose health endpoints and you can configure circuit breakers and rate limits. We'll share the exact endpoints and examples.

[00:09:51] Jordan: Regarding compliance, do you have any certified penetration test results we can review?

[00:09:56] Ivy: We can share a redacted pentest summary as part of the security packet.

[00:10:03] Elena: Anything else from Redwood?

[00:10:06] Maya: Nothing else — I want to leave time for open Qs.

[00:10:10] Samir: Quick one — do you support model version pinning and automatic rollbacks if a model underperforms? That was a pain point with our old vendor.

[00:10:19] Carlos: Yes, we support model versioning and rollout policies. Canary with automatic rollback on quality regressions or latency SLO failures is built-in.

[00:10:30] Elena: Great.

[00:10:35] [later in call; timeline planning]
[00:21:02] Maya: Ok, walking through the onboarding checklist now — account setup, IdP, KMS, region selection, token scopes, test dataset, and bench schedule. We'll put owners and dates on each item.

[00:32:47] Carlos: Technical deep-dive request — Priya, can you give us a brief of your network topology so we can pre-validate peering?

[00:32:53] Priya: We have a mixed multi-account AWS setup in us-west-2 with strict egress controls and a private NAT. We'll send a topology diagram.

[00:40:10] Carlos: Noted. For KV cache usage — if you can provide expected prefix patterns that helps set cache sizing.

[00:40:18] Samir: We'll get that to you.

[00:45:05] Maya: Recap and next steps: 1) Redwood to send onboarding packet (Ivy) and SOW (Maya) by 2027-03-07; 2) Aurora to review and sign SOW by 2027-03-09 to meet trial timeline; 3) Carlos to provision Dedicated trial and run benchmark plan week of 2027-03-15; 4) Schedule a technical deep-dive for Priya's team — propose 2027-03-10 or 2027-03-11.

[00:45:40] Elena: Let's lock 2027-03-11 for the deep-dive.

[00:45:45] Ivy: I'll send calendar invite after the call.

[00:46:00] Jordan: Thanks, please include the redacted pentest and SOC2 in the packet.

[00:46:06] Ivy: Will do.

[00:46:18] Maya: Any final questions?

[00:46:22] Samir: No, this is good.

[00:46:26] Elena: All good from product.

[00:46:30] Priya: Ok.

[00:46:34] Maya: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and the SOW and that should get things moving.

[00:46:45] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings in names and acronyms; speaker labels approximate.
